answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can make reputation grow slowly through useful work, the way a garden grows only after seasons of tending. New identities start at the jetty, with limited access to shared resources, and must prove reliability over time before earning deeper trust. Like a glacier, trust moves slowly and is hard to fake in bulk: an attacker can spawn a thousand names, but cannot cheaply manufacture long histories of consistent, verified service. Let peers vouch only with their own stake at risk, so each new sock-puppet costs more than the value it can extract.
